issues.description: Path references contain placeholder '~/Hello-World' which assumes Unix-like environments and specific directory structure. This reduces portability across different operating systems and user setups.
issues.suggestion: Use relative paths or provide platform-specific instructions. Consider documenting platform compatibility at the top of the README.

issues.description: The output example contains hardcoded path '/Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/' which is platform-specific (macOS) and may mislead Windows or Linux users.
issues.suggestion: Either remove the hardcoded output example or indicate that paths are platform-specific and show examples for multiple operating systems.

issues.description: Missing newline at end of file. The file ends with '$ touch README' without a trailing newline character.

suggestions.description: Separate command documentation from command execution with descriptive headings
suggestions.before:
$ mkdir ~/Hello-WorldCreates a directory for your project called "Hello-World" in your user directory
$ cd ~/Hello-WorldChanges the current working directory to your newly created directory
$ git initSets up the necessary Git files
Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/
$ touch README
suggestions.after:
## Setup Instructions

### 1. Create Project Directory
```bash
$ mkdir ~/Hello-World
```
Creates a directory for your project called "Hello-World" in your user directory

### 2. Navigate to Project
```bash
$ cd ~/Hello-World
```
Changes the current working directory to your newly created directory

### 3. Initialize Git Repository
```bash
$ git init
```
Sets up the necessary Git files. You should see:
```
Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/
```

### 4. Create README
```bash
$ touch README
```
